source_snapshot.items: PMIC Fatal Error - Critical Temp Shutdown
source_snapshot.procedure: Uses a split railtype7/voltagetype0/dimm0 tuple, says reset immediately, and repeats all DIMMs with voltage types0/1 after changing PMIC, SPD/telemetry and I2C settings.
source_snapshot.criteria: Uncorrectable PASS and OS report, with neither a thermal threshold nor an authoritative shutdown/reset timeline.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic critical/temperature text does not prove a synthetic PMIC thermal latch or safe physical temperature.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Adds monitoring but does not resolve shutdown versus reset, voltage parameters on a thermal fault, threshold/hysteresis or cooldown.

old_problem: The title mandates critical-temperature shutdown while the procedure says immediate reset; railtype7, voltage-type applicability, synthetic threshold/latch/clear semantics, sensor/I2C mapping, no-real-heating limits and restart recovery are unauthoritative.
disposition_reason: This conflict changes both the stimulus and terminal power action and cannot be parameterized safely. ED-06/12/15/16/18 require separate, authoritative cycle semantics, PASS limits and recovery; the review therefore preserves the case as Pending/BLOCKED and explicitly forbids real heating.
decision_basis: Directly read Reliability row93/history2491 and checked that adjacent railtype4/5 cases are voltage-input domains, not thermal substitutes.
Preserved all-DIMM intent, railtype7 literal, disputed voltage selectors, PMIC settings, power action and OS evidence.
Separated injected thermal status from actual sensor temperature and required independent physical-temperature proof.
Required an approved latch-clear/cooldown and controlled restart before memory validation.
No command inference, heating, injection, reset, power-on, retry or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Synthetic DDR5 PMIC critical-temperature shutdown protection
test_case.purpose: Inject an approved synthetic critical-temperature condition into each mapped PMIC, prove the correct thermal latch and protective power action while actual hardware remains within safe temperature, then clear, cool, restart and restore memory safely.
required_package: Vendor proof for railtype7 and whether voltage-type parameters are valid
Critical threshold, hysteresis, latch/status/clear and physical-temperature safety limits
Per-DIMM PMIC thermal-sensor/address and Wistron I2C/OOB topology
Approved decision and timing for shutdown, reset or staged action
Exact synthetic tuple matrix, cooldown/restart gates, evidence oracle and rollback
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the source tuple or heat hardware. After authority is approved, record actual PMIC/DIMM/ambient temperatures, fans, power, status and memory; issue one synthetic thermal tuple under OOB monitoring; observe the signed power action and latched thermal source; clear/cool and restart only through the approved sequence, then restore settings and validate all memory.
test_case.expected_result: The intended PMIC records the signed synthetic critical-temperature status, physical temperatures stay inside the hard safety envelope, the host performs exactly the approved shutdown/reset sequence, and after authorized clear/cooldown/restart all sensors, fans, DIMMs, memory and configuration return healthy.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires a target-specific thermal latch, safe real temperatures, the exact authorized power timeline, complete cooldown/clear evidence and post-restart memory recovery. Generic logs, real heating, unexplained voltage selector, wrong action, restart loop, lost DIMM or missing restoration is FAIL/BLOCKED.
safety_gate: Synthetic fault injection only; never raise physical temperature to reach the threshold.
Independent OOB power, fan and temperature monitoring with hard aborts.
One mapped PMIC once; no automatic restart or target loop.
Abort on actual temperature rise, wrong sensor/status, unexpected power behavior, management loss or training failure.
expected_evidence: Railtype7 thermal threshold/hysteresis/latch/clear and power-action specification
PMIC/DIMM thermal-sensor and BMC I2C/OOB map
Exact synthetic tuple and OOB shutdown/reset chronology
Fresh thermal PMIC plus CPER/BERT/SEL source evidence with no real excursion
Latch clear, cooldown, authorized restart, full DIMM/memory/fan health and restoration diff
test_case.recovery: Keep the host off if temperature or latch state is unsafe. Under engineer control, clear the synthetic latch, confirm approved cooldown and stable fans/sensors, restore PMIC recovery, SPD/telemetry, I2C and BIOS/HDT settings, then start once and verify all memory. No automatic recovery.

source_conflict.reason: Critical-temperature shutdown conflicts with immediate reset; thermal meaning of voltage types, target expansion, thresholds and action timing remain undefined.

blocked.reason: Ambiguous thermal stimulus/action can mask a real over-temperature condition, cause repeated power cycling or restart before a PMIC latch is safely cleared.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Synthetic thermal selector/parameters, thresholds, sensor/I2C topology, shutdown-versus-reset decision, cooldown/restart evidence and recovery.
pending.execution_status: ENGINEERING DECISION RETAINED; BLOCKED; NO DUT ACTION EXECUTED

pending.unlock_condition: Approve a synthetic-only thermal stimulus and complete threshold, power-action, cooldown and recovery contract.

project_authority: Vendor PMIC thermal semantics and Wistron platform power/BMC policies govern the synthetic latch, physical limits and restart sequence.
